video.title: I Let Strangers Pitch Me Their Business Live

summary: The Koerner Office hosts a live pitch event in Utah. Ten strangers get 2 minutes to pitch and 10 minutes of critique from Chris Koerner, Nick and Brandon. The pitches range from an operating VA-funded massage business doing about $68k/month and a $1.5M ARR home-service marketing agency to pre-revenue ideas such as a seed cup, an NFC keychain, a containment diaper, a choose-your-path kids' letter subscription, an AI relationship app and mail-in cast iron cleaning. The hosts invested in or offered to help several, and the audience voted Go Seeds first, Pick a Path Letters second and Utah Veterans Massage third. The main takeaways are that distribution (especially paid ads and short-form video) is the recurring bottleneck, and that investors want proof of a repeatable process before funding. All numbers are unverified pitch claims.

speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; runs the live pitch event and offers small investments.

ideas.name: Utah Veterans Massage
ideas.one_liner: Licensed therapists treat veterans in small leased rooms, paid about $90 per session by the VA via TriWest under a 12-free-session benefit.
ideas.business_model: Per-session insurance reimbursement (VA via TriWest); therapists paid per session.
ideas.customer: Veterans eligible for 12 VA-paid massage sessions; the VA refers by geographic proximity.
ideas.problem: Veterans in pain need access to medical massage that the VA funds, and new therapists struggle to find well-paid work.
ideas.offer: Medical and deep-tissue massage in one or two-room clinics, with billing, insurance back end and scheduling handled by the company.

pricing.model: VA reimbursement per session; therapist paid about $50
pricing.notes: Rates vary by state; the founder says they never go below about $89.

acquisition_channels.details: The VA (via TriWest) calls the company based on proximity to the veteran, so many small locations get referrals. No marketing spend. Getting into the network took about 8 months.

quote.text: we haven't spent a single dollar on marketing. The reason we have so many small office locations instead of one central is the VA will call us based on the geographic proximity to the veteran
quote.speaker: Aean Harden

ideas.delivery: Employed or contracted therapists treat clients in leased clinics (about $500-650/month rent each); therapists rebook clients at the end of each session; staff handle billing, insurance and scheduling.
unit_economics_claims: Credentialing automated with AI, about 25 minutes per person
tools: AI automation for credentialing and paperwork
ideas.startup_cost: not stated (rented a room one day a week to begin)
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: about 8 months to get into the VA network; first rented room 18 months before the pitch

acquisition.how: VA referrals are inbound and need no marketing, but credentialing each new state is a gate.

onboarding.how: AI-automated credentialing is claimed to take 25 minutes per therapist; client booking comes via VA referral.

delivery.how: Hands-on massage by a licensed therapist in a physical clinic.

billing.how: Insurance back-end billing is claimed to be automated with AI and software; payer rules vary by state.

support.how: Schedulers (the founder's wife plus one) handle rebooking and queries with scheduling software.

uk_applicability.notes: Depends on the US VA/TriWest benefit and Medicaid-style rates. The UK has no equivalent per-session funded benefit, and NHS veterans' services are commissioned differently. Massage therapy would also need UK registration and insurance.

risks: Revenue depends on a single payer (VA/TriWest)
Each state differs in licensing, credentialing and pre-authorisation, so expansion may lag
Founder admits to a 'grow, expand and then figure it out' approach
Owner-operator bottleneck; needs a COO or operations manager
Valuation ask of $2M was seen as too high

quotes.text: we did 750 sessions a month. So revenue is 68,000 and 20,000 of that about is profit.
quotes.speaker: Aean Harden

quotes.text: I'm looking for 100,000 for a 5% uh equity stake and also a partner who's taken a healthcare business multi-state ideally.
quotes.speaker: Aean Harden

ideas.name: Go Seeds
ideas.one_liner: A dual-compartment disposable cup that holds sunflower seeds on one side and spit shells on the other, sold at about $5.
ideas.business_model: One-off product sales (convenience stores, with possible reusable and branded editions and a licensing/partnership route).
ideas.customer: Sunflower seed eaters, e.g. dads in cars, sold through gas stations and convenience stores.
ideas.problem: Eating sunflower seeds creates a shell mess in cars and homes.
ideas.offer: A packaged cup with seeds in one chamber and a shell compartment on the other end; possible Go Nuts variant.

price_points.label: gas station price of equivalent seeds
claimed cost at scale incl. seeds (transcript reads '$120')

pricing.notes: Priced at a premium to a standard bag of seeds.

acquisition_channels.details: Aimed at gas stations and convenience stores, where seeds are a top seller; Brandon suggested Facebook ads.

quote.text: Hands down, it's sunflower seeds. Next is beer. But sunflower seeds are have a great throughput.
quote.speaker: Cam Finley

acquisition_channels.details: Brandon offered to help with Facebook ads.

ideas.delivery: Manufactured and filled by a third party (not yet set up); sold through retail.
unit_economics_claims: Cost about $1.20 per filled cup (transcript garbled)
Retail target under $5 vs $3.20 gas station seeds

acquisition.how: Retail placement needs relationships, though paid social could run with agents.

delivery.how: Physical manufacturing, filling and logistics through third parties.

support.how: Simple product with low support needs.

uk_applicability.notes: Product works in UK convenience stores, though seed consumption is lower than in the US. Food packaging rules and a UK patent filing would apply.

risks: Manufacturing at a $1.20 cost with seeds is unverified
Low barriers to copying; patent only provisional

quotes.text: You can get a pack of seeds, the same amount of seeds. You can get it for $3.20 at a gas station.
quotes.speaker: Cam Finley

quotes.text: I'm asking for a strategic partnership. That's what I want.
quotes.speaker: Cam Finley

ideas.name: NFC lost-person keychains (Next to Kin)
ideas.one_liner: Cheap 3D-printed NFC tags that anyone can tap to call a lost child or dementia patient's contact, sold to institutions and events at about $5 each.
ideas.business_model: B2B bulk sales to institutions and events; possible recurring add-on suggested by hosts.
ideas.customer: Event organisers, football clubs, dementia-care facilities and charities such as the Alzheimer Society.
ideas.problem: Children and people with dementia or autism get lost and strangers cannot easily help.
ideas.offer: A free-to-use NFC tag with no app, battery, subscription or tracking, tapped by any phone to reach a caregiver.

pricing.model: Per-unit sales to institutions, minimum 5,000-unit orders
pricing.notes: The founder hands them out free to the public as advertising.

acquisition_channels.details: Events, sports teams (Saskatchewan Roughriders) and institutions; national news coverage in Canada; Alzheimer Society of Ontario picking it up.

quote.text: This has gotten really big traction up in Canada. It's made national news.
quote.speaker: Tom Hamilton

ideas.delivery: 3D-printed tags with NFC chips made by the founder, shipped in large orders.
unit_economics_claims: 30-40 cents to make, $5 each to institutions
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: not stated (about a year since the idea)

acquisition.how: Large institutional and event deals need relationship-building.

onboarding.how: Bulk orders are simple, though custom shapes are human work.

delivery.how: 3D printing and shipping are physical work.

uk_applicability.notes: NFC tags and event tie-ins work in the UK. Charity and care-home sales and GDPR on the linked data need care; UK has similar missing-person charities.

risks: Behaviour-change product with institutional sales cycles
Competes with AirTags in buyers' minds
Visa motive: founder wants an E2 visa

quotes.text: right now I'm making about 10 grand a month
quotes.speaker: Tom Hamilton

quotes.text: They're $5 each. The hard cost is somewhere about 40 cents each to make.
quotes.speaker: Tom Hamilton

ideas.name: Secure Pocket containment adult brief
ideas.one_liner: A patented double-layer adult diaper with a pocket for heavy output; currently hand-sewn and pre-revenue, seeking $300k via SAFE.
ideas.business_model: One-off product sales or licensing to large manufacturers/distributors.
ideas.customer: Care facilities, caregivers and heavy-incontinence users.
ideas.problem: Standard adult diapers leak with heavy output.
ideas.offer: A double-layer brief with a containment pocket.

acquisition_channels.details: Lead investor in healthcare; Nick suggested licensing or selling to a large manufacturer.

ideas.delivery: Hand-sewn so far; a facility was found to produce at scale, though machines cost $1M-3M.
unit_economics_claims: Asks $300k via SAFE, $65k for a machine
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: not stated (soft launched two weeks earlier)

acquisition.how: Selling into care facilities and distributors is relationship-led.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK with medical device and hygiene compliance; the patent is US.

risks: Two businesses at once (design and manufacturing)
Dominant incumbents with machines costing millions

quotes.text: We do not. We are pre-revenue.
quotes.speaker: Nisha

quotes.text: 300,000 in total 65,000 for the machine this time.
quotes.speaker: Nisha

ideas.name: Pick a Path Letters
ideas.one_liner: Subscription of illustrated story letters mailed twice a month where the child chooses what happens next.
ideas.business_model: Subscription and prepaid story bundles, with physical mail fulfilment.
ideas.problem: Kids love mail and parents want reading and critical-thinking activities.
ideas.offer: One chapter per letter, with a choice at the end, coloring pages and an optional gift bundle with a book.

acquisition_channels.details: Meta ads test spending about $1,000-1,500 to get 10 customers; the founders say they lack social media and ads skills.

quote.text: I think we spent a,000 or 1,500 bucks, and that's how we got 10 customers
quote.speaker: Cameron

ideas.delivery: Professionally written and illustrated letters mailed; choices collected through texts or a QR page automated via Go High Level.
unit_economics_claims: 75-80% margins on the bundle, about 85% monthly (mostly shipping)
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: first letters sent in January (about a year before)

acquisition.how: Paid ads and organic video can be driven by agents.

onboarding.how: Go High Level automation handles sign-up and reminders.

delivery.how: Printing and posting are physical but can use print-on-demand and mail houses.

uk_applicability.notes: UK has a similar subscription kids' mail market; Royal Mail postage and children's data need GDPR care.

risks: Customer acquisition unsolved; only 23 subscribers after a year
No AI-written content promise limits scalability

quotes.text: we're using go high level right now for our CRM automation
quotes.speaker: Cameron

quotes.text: So for the bundle our margins are about what was it 80 75 to 80%.
quotes.speaker: Cameron

ideas.name: Doghouse app
ideas.one_liner: AI relationship assistant for husbands that nudges and drafts thoughtful messages based on knowledge of the partner.
ideas.problem: Men forget to plan, remember or act on important moments for their partner.
ideas.offer: A web app (built on Base44) with an AI coach that knows the partner's preferences and sends nudges.

pricing.notes: Cost depends on LLM token usage.

acquisition_channels.details: Brandon suggests copying Facebook ads of a men's dance-teaching company via the Meta ads library.

ideas.delivery: Web app using LLMs, with data onboarding via Gmail/Outlook and texts.

acquisition.how: Ads and content can be automated.

uk_applicability.notes: Works the same; GDPR consent for reading messages is required.

ideas.business_model: Per-item service fee (suggested pivot to content plus product).

ideas.offer: Mail in cookware, receive it cleaned and seasoned.

unit_economics_claims: Shipping about $15 each way per Brandon

ideas.name: Goodly
ideas.one_liner: Marketing agency for home service businesses selling websites and Google Business Profile management at about $450/month.
ideas.customer: Owner-operator home service businesses doing $300k-$1.5M revenue.
ideas.problem: Small home service firms need web presence and inbound leads.
ideas.offer: Websites, Google Business Profile management, some SEO, and paid ads.

pricing.notes: About $10k of MRR is paid ads.

acquisition_channels.details: All customers acquired by cold calling, with SDRs overseas; remote sales not great, wants in-person office.

quote.text: primarily we're all cold calling. That's how we get our customers.
quote.speaker: James Lincoln

ideas.delivery: Team with AI agents for on-page optimisation, onboarding, Google Business Profile posts and pages.

acquisition.how: Cold calling can be partially automated, but UK TPS/CTPS rules apply; sole traders are restricted.

delivery.how: AI agents handle on-page SEO and GBP tasks.

uk_applicability.notes: UK agency model works; cold calls need TPS screening and sole traders are restricted.

tactics.name: Use a payer-referred niche with guaranteed volume
steps: Find populations whose services are pre-paid by a third party (e.g. VA 12 free sessions)
Join the payer network, accept referrals by proximity
Open many small leased rooms near referrals instead of one big site

quote.text: the VA will call us based on the geographic proximity to the veteran and so we have a lot of little ones
quote.speaker: Aean Harden

tactics.name: Offload therapist admin
steps: Therapists only deliver and rebook the next session
Central staff handle billing, insurance and scheduling
Use scheduling software to cut admin

tactics.name: Free hand-out as advertising, sell to institutions
steps: Give tags free (30-40 cents cost)
Sell at $5 to institutions with minimum 5,000-unit orders
Optionally add a $1/month recurring option

tactics.name: Automate customer choices with text and QR
steps: Text parents reminders via Go High Level
Accept replies or a QR code web form
Use choice to select the next chapter

tactics.name: Pay-to-scale ads
steps: Treat ads as a learnable skill
Reinvest from $1,500 (10 customers) to larger spend
Study competitors in the Meta ads library

quote.text: your next 1,500 will get 30 customers and your next will get 60
quote.speaker: Brandon

tactics.name: Test with milestones before investing
steps: Reach 50 paying customers
Churn below 15%
App store approval before raising

quote.text: call it 50 paying customers with your churn under 15%
quote.speaker: Nick

tactics.name: Content-first pivot
steps: Film time-lapse before and after videos
Post consistently on short-form platforms
Monetise with product or sponsorship once reach is proven

warnings.warning: Expanding state by state means different licensing and credentialing and payer rules; do not just hire an ops manager and figure it out.

quote.text: every state's going to be different
quote.speaker: Nick

warnings.warning: In-home healthcare is hard; prefer clinic-based delivery.

quote.text: Friends don't let friends offer healthcare in the home.
quote.speaker: Nick

warnings.warning: Do not go to investors with an idea and no plan or numbers.

quote.text: just have a business plan, right?
quote.speaker: Brandon

warnings.warning: Do not invest in your own learning with outside money; show that you have tried and burned money first.

quote.text: I'm not trying to build the fire with your money.
quote.speaker: Brandon

warnings.warning: Mailing heavy items can cost more than the service fee.

quote.text: shipping those is going to cost like 15 bucks each way
quote.speaker: Brandon

lessons.lesson: A payer-guaranteed customer pool removes CAC risk but creates concentration risk.

quote.text: he's going after the VA in particular is cuz they're guaranteeing a certain number
quote.speaker: Nick

lessons.lesson: Changing the form factor of an everyday product can create a standout offer.

quote.text: So I'm all in on a new form factor.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Investors back the founder as much as the idea, so come prepared with specifics.

quote.text: I'm really investing in you
quote.speaker: Brandon

lessons.lesson: Distribution is the main bottleneck for subscription and app ideas; learn paid ads yourself.

quote.text: You got to learn the ads yourself because that is how this entire business grows.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Profitable cash-flowing businesses may not need outside capital unless they have a proven funnel to scale.
Telling a story and involving family helps pitches resonate and attract help.

quote.text: I like to say sell your story.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Low-ticket $450/month service businesses can reach $1.5M ARR with high margins if churn is spread across many customers.
LLM-based apps need token cost control and distribution plans because they are easy to copy.
Do not just consume content; start something and earn revenue.

quote.text: go start something. Go do something.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: Live pitches with mostly unverified first-hand claims (e.g. Utah Veterans Massage and Goodly give specific numbers) mixed with idea-stage pitches with no data. The format is entertainment with hosts also acting as potential investors; claims are not audited.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Chris Koerner sells a $5/month community and a sponsor read for Beehiiv appears; hosts have investments or competing businesses (Brandon owns a Goodly competitor).
